newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Lyons wants to keep top U.S. forest job.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Lyons wants to keep top U.S. forest job.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Undersecretary Jim Lyons said Tuesday he wants to retain his post as overseer of the national forest system in a second Clinton administration.

"That's up to the president," Lyons said when asked if he would remain in his job, one of the top environmental posts in the federal government. He said he would be happy to serve in the second term if asked.
As undersecretary, Lyons is in charge of 191 million acres of U.S. forests, including timber sales, as well as running soil and water conservation programs.
